1.note: An earlier emissary from the Land of Israel, given only by an abbreviated name; not identified.

2.note: Read as "and here" (ופה); the abbreviation mark is not explained.

3.note: So printed. 15 Shevat 5537 was a Thursday, so Friday night falls on 16 to 17 Shevat; טו"ב is probably a misprint for ט"ז (16).

4.note: Family names of Trieste Jews, given as printed; not identified.

5.note: The entry gives no year or place. Shelaḥ was read on 28 June 1777, between the Ḥida's stay in Mantua (May) and his arrival in Avignon (30 July); the dates in brackets assume that year.

6.note: "Between them" is not explained in the entry; it may refer to a quarrel told elsewhere.

8.note: So the 1885 printing (ט"ו = 15). A. Freimann, Ma'agal Tov ha-Shalem (Berlin–Jerusalem 1921–34), p. 120, reads מ"ו (46); in this type ט and מ are easily confused, and 15 miles is the likelier figure.

9.he: סי' פאבר"י ... מהקאדימייא די לה סינסייא
9.note: "Fabri" of the Académie des Sciences: not identified.

10.note: 26 Kislev 5538 was itself a Friday. "The sixth day" may be the same day, a week later (2 January 1778), or the sixth day of Hanukkah (30 Kislev, Tuesday 30 December 1777).

11.note: Printed רז"כיר; read אזכיר, "I will recount" (Isa 63:7), as A. Freimann, Ma'agal Tov ha-Shalem (Berlin–Jerusalem 1921–34), p. 121, prints it.

12.he: שבעה שרי צרפת ... ד' קהלות דמיץ, מונטשפלייר, פיזינאס, כרבונא
12.note: The 1885 printing reads "seven princes (שרי) of France" and דמיץ; A. Freimann, Ma'agal Tov ha-Shalem (Berlin–Jerusalem 1921–34), p. 121, reads שבעת ערי צרפת, "seven cities of France", and נימיץ, Nîmes, which the list of cities needs (ע/ש and נ/ד misread). "The four communities" are the four papal communities of the Comtat (Avignon, Carpentras, Cavaillon, L'Isle), where these Jews came from; כרבונא is Narbonne.
